THE FRENCH WORD “ANIMALIER” in the title of Dan Ostermiller Animalier: Celebrating 50 Years of Sculpting, the new exhibition at Nedra Matteucci Galleries in Santa Fe, New Mexico, hints at the European origins of the genre of artwork that Ostermiller has made his own for half a century. The desire for realism that permeated human depiction in the arts in the 19th century migrated to the natural world—and to animals specifically—at the same time. Opening on June 26 and running through July 17, this solo exhibition will feature Ostermiller’s earlier works as well as 10 new pieces. Ostermiller was born and grew up in Cheyenne, Wyoming. Santa Fe is one of the leading art centers in the Southwest, known for its high concentration of galleries and long-established arts community. Canyon Road is the city's most well-known gallery area, with additional clusters in the Plaza / Downtown and Railyard districts. Nedra Matteucci Galleries is a must-visit for art enthusiasts, boasting an extensive collection of American art from the 19th and 20th centuries. The gallery features works by renowned artists such as the Taos Society of Artists, American West artists, and masters of American Impressionism and Modernism. Visitors can also explore the Gaugy Gallery showcasing a variety of Jean-Claude Gaugy's signature carved wood paintings.
